headline: Jharkhand youth jailed in Dubai for four months; family seeks Indian government help to secure his return
content: Medininagar A 23-year-old man from Jharkhand's Palamu district has been in a UAE jail for four months now, with his father complaining to police in Medininagar that his son was incarcerated for leaving his job without properly informing the company and paying a tout to return home. The youth's father, Lalan Paswan of Dadra village, submitted an application at the Hussinabad police station on Monday (October 26, 2026), urging the Palamu district administration to bring his son Shashi Kumar Paswan back, Superintendent of Police Kapil Choudhary told PTI. "My son went to Dubai in 2025 to work in a private company on contract. The family had fixed his sister's wedding for June 26, and Shashi wanted to attend it. He paid an agent to return home, but was trapped," the aggrieved father said. A police official said, "Shashi is in jail for allegedly contacting the agent, giving him money to return home and leaving his job without properly informing the company. He was absent from work for seven consecutive days." Lalan Paswan said his son has been lodged in a jail in Dubai's Al Rashidiya for the past four months. "Shashi assured us that he will come out of the jail soon. Based on his assurance, the family waited for over four months before reporting the matter. I urge the administration and the Government of India to take necessary action and bring my son back," he said. The Superintendent of Police of Palamu said the application has been forwarded to higher authorities. Shashi Paswan’s wife, Sumitra, said, "My husband was hired by a private company in Abu Dhabi on a contract basis. He has been trapped by the agent and has been in jail for the past four months. I urge the authorities to provide him legal help and bring him home."

headline: Census 2027: Every Person Must Be Counted, Says Meghalaya Chief Secretary
content: Meghalaya Chief Secretary Dr Shakil P. Ahammed, today stressed the importance of comprehensive population data for inclusive development and effective implementation of government welfare schemes, urging officers to ensure that every individual is counted in Census 2027. He was addressing a State-Level Training Conference of Principal Census Officers and senior officers on Phase II (Population Enumeration) of Census 2027, held at the State Guest House, Taraghar, Shillong. The conference aimed to strengthen operational preparedness, coordination and public awareness ahead of the enumeration exercise. Emphasising that the census was far more than a headcount, Ahammed said reliable demographic and socio-economic data would help the government identify gaps in healthcare, education, social welfare, road connectivity and digital infrastructure. The information would also support Meghalaya’s development vision for 2032 and help assess progress towards the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). Highlighting the state’s geographical diversity, predominantly rural settlements and tribal population, the Chief Secretary noted that these factors presented unique challenges for census operations. He stressed that people living in remote areas, including Baghmara, Dalu and Ranikor, must be covered, warning that incomplete data could lead to gaps in public services and leave vulnerable communities outside the reach of government programmes. He urged officers to publicise the census and its importance to sensitise the public and encourage participation. Ahammed also underlined the role of population data in strengthening Meghalaya’s investment prospects by providing insights into demographic trends, market potential, youth capabilities and infrastructure requirements. As the state pursues its ambition of building a $10-billion economy and subsequently a $16-billion economy, he said such information would be crucial for long-term economic planning and attracting private investment. The Chief Secretary commended the State Nodal Officer, officers of the Office of the Registrar General of India (ORGI) and nearly 10,000 personnel, including enumerators, for successfully completing the House Listing and Housing Census phase despite numerous challenges. Expressing confidence in the team’s ability to build on this experience, he called upon census personnel to discharge their responsibilities with diligence and commitment.

headline: Theon Group Acquires Maneesh Pharma Unit VI, Renames Facility Zoevita Lifesciences
content: Theon Group said the acquisition would support its manufacturing requirements and create opportunities to serve domestic and international markets.Theon Group has acquired Maneesh Pharma’s Unit VI in Baddi, Himachal Pradesh, through a slump sale, expanding its pharmaceutical manufacturing operations. The acquired facility will operate as Zoevita Lifesciences Ltd., adding manufacturing capacity for pharmaceutical and nutraceutical products across tablets, capsules and sachets.The facility has an annual production capacity of 3,000 million tablets, 150 million capsules and 30 million sachets. Theon Group said the acquisition would support its manufacturing requirements and create opportunities to serve domestic and international markets.Zoevita Lifesciences holds World Health Organization Good Manufacturing Practices (WHO-GMP) certification, according to the company’s credentials. Its stated international regulatory approvals or market authorizations cover Ethiopia, Tanzania, Uganda, Uzbekistan, Myanmar and Yemen. The company also references US Food and Drug Administration (USFDA) and European Union (EU) compliance expectations.Located in Baddi, a major pharmaceutical manufacturing hub in India, the facility is designed to support production efficiency, product quality and growing customer requirements.Plans to Expand Manufacturing CapabilitiesZoevita is planning to add oral liquid manufacturing sections to its existing operations. The proposed expansion would broaden its dosage-form capabilities across pharmaceutical and nutraceutical products.The acquisition adds another operating company to Theon Group’s portfolio, which includes Theon Pharmaceuticals Ltd., Theon Lifesciences Ltd. and Theogen Pvt. Ltd. Zoevita Lifesciences Ltd. will now join these businesses as part of the group’s pharmaceutical manufacturing operations.Theon Group operates across pharmaceutical manufacturing and generic medicines. The acquisition expands its manufacturing footprint in Baddi and adds production capacity across multiple dosage forms.The company has not disclosed the financial terms of the slump sale.

headline: HRTC to Run 266 Additional Buses from Delhi, Chandigarh and Baddi for Diwali
content: Shimla: The Himachal Road Transport Corporation (HRTC) will operate 266 additional buses from Delhi, Chandigarh and Baddi to various destinations across Himachal Pradesh to facilitate the movement of passengers returning home for Diwali. According to the corporation, 134 additional bus services will operate on November 6, followed by 132 services on November 7. The special arrangements have been made in view of the expected surge in passenger traffic during the festive season to reduce overcrowding and ensure convenient travel. On November 6, HRTC will operate 42 additional buses from Delhi, 69 from Chandigarh and 23 from Baddi to different destinations in the state. Similarly, on November 7, a total of 49 additional buses will depart from Delhi, 63 from Chandigarh and 20 from Baddi. The corporation has made these arrangements to help passengers reach their hometowns in time for the festival and manage the increased demand for public transport. Meanwhile, HRTC’s local bus services will remain suspended from 5 pm on November 8 until 8 am on November 9, covering Diwali evening and the early hours of the following day.

headline: Himachal Congress, BJP spar over electoral rolls | Hindustan Times
content: The Congress and the Bharatiya Janata Party in Himachal Pradesh traded charges over democracy, the Constitution, and the impartiality of constitutional institutions in the country.The state Congress chief Vinay Kumar accused the BJP of weakening democratic institutions, while BJP state president Rajeev Bindal alleged that the Congress and the INDI Alliance were attempting to create an atmosphere of political instability and anarchy in the country.Vinay said serious questions are being raised about the state of democracy and the impartiality of constitutional institutions in the country, but instead of addressing these concerns, the BJP was indulging in a blame game with the Congress.“If anyone has fostered chaos in the nation, it is the BJP; if anyone has weakened democracy, it is the BJP; and if the core spirit of the Constitution has been undermined, it is a direct consequence of the BJP’s policies and style of governance. Now, in an attempt to shirk its political responsibilities, the BJP is pointing fingers at the Congress,” Vinay said in a statement. He expressed concerns regarding the large-scale removal of names from electoral rolls and said no eligible citizen should be wrongfully excluded from the voter lists.Responding to charges, Bindal alleged that the Congress, after repeatedly facing rejection by voters, was seeking to create chaos in the country to bring about a change of government through unconstitutional means.“The Congress has repeatedly undermined constitutional principles while publicly projecting itself as their defender,” he said, raising the issue of illegal immigration. He claimed that such vote-bank politics threatened the rights of legitimate Indian citizens.Announcing a statewide public awareness campaign, Bindal said the BJP would organise four marches under the banner ‘Save Democracy, Remove Anarchy’ across Himachal Pradesh. The first foot march will take place in Dharamshala on October 30, followed by one in Shimla on November 1, and marches in Mandi and Hamirpur on November 4.
